sources.entry: jsonschema - An implementation of JSON Schema for Python.

summary.one_liner: jsonschema is a Python implementation of the JSON Schema specification for validating JSON data against schemas.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a validate() function that raises a ValidationError when an instance does not match a schema, and returns silently when it does. Supports Draft 2020-12, 2019-09, 7, 6, 4 and 3 of the JSON Schema specification. Offers lazy validation that can iteratively report all validation errors. Allows programmatic querying of which properties or items failed validation. Has optional "format" and "format-nongpl" extras for format-related dependencies, though format checks are not activated just by installing them or listing formats in a schema. The README also points to check-jsonschema for command-line use.
use_cases: validate JSON data against a schema in Python
check API payloads or config files against a JSON Schema
report all validation errors in a JSON document
find which fields or items failed JSON validation
validate JSON against older drafts such as Draft 4 or Draft 7
how_to_run: from jsonschema import validate; validate(instance=data, schema=schema)
notable: Lazy validation that can yield all errors, not just the first
Programmatic querying of failing properties or items
Optional format extras, with a non-GPL variant
Command-line use available via the separate check-jsonschema project
caveats: Format validation is off by default and must be enabled explicitly, per the specification
Command-line usage requires installing the separate check-jsonschema package
README does not state platform or Python version requirements beyond the PyPI badge
